body.p: Claims 1-21 are pending. Claims 1, 3, 4, 8, 10, 11, 15, 17, and 18 are amended. Claim 21 is newly added and claims 2, 9, and 16 are canceled. No new matter has been added by way of the amendments.

The Office Action rejected claims 1-5, 7-12, and 14-19 under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2021/0279968 to Eathakota et al. (hereinafter "Eathakota").

The Office Action rejected claims 1-20 on the grounds of non-statutory double patenting as being unpatentable over claims 1-20 of U.S. Patent No. 11,266,907 and claims 1-20 of U.S. Patent No. 11,707,677.
Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections for at least the reasons discussed below.

Applicant thanks the Office for the indication that claims 6, 13, and 20 would be allowable if amended into independent form. Applicant has elected to pursue different amendments at this time, but reserves the right to pursue such allowable subject matter at a later date.

The Office Action rejected claims 1-20 on the grounds of non-statutory double patenting as being unpatentable over claims 1-20 of U.S. Patent No. 11,266,907 and claims 1-20 of U.S. Patent No. 11,707,677. Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections for at least the reasons discussed below.

A terminal disclaimer over U.S. Pat. Nos. 11,266,907 and 11,707,677 is filed herewith. Withdrawal of the non-statutory obviousness-type double patenting rejections is respectfully requested in light of the terminal disclaimer filed herewith.
The Office Action rejected claims 1-5, 7-12, and 14-19 under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being
unpatentable over Eathakota. Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections for at least the reasons discussed below.
Amended claim 1 recites:
A visualization system comprising: a display;
at least one accelerometer that is fixed with respect to the display; one or more processors; and
one or more storage devices storing computer-executable instructions which, when executed by the one or more processors, cause
the one or more processors to:

p.u: cause one or more images of a real-world electronic gaming machine to be obtained, match the real-world electronic gaming machine to a corresponding virtual electronic gaming machine in a catalogue of virtual electronic gaming machines,

body.p: cause the display to present a representation of a real-world location,

cause, responsive to changes in orientation of the display evident from data from the one or more accelerometers, a perspective of the representation of the real-world location to be modified, [[and]]

add, responsive to receipt of user input, one or more instances of the corresponding virtual electronic gaming machine[[s]] to the representation of the real-world location, wherein the displayed representation of the real-world location and the one or more instances of the corresponding virtual electronic gaming machine[[s]] generate a mixed reality gaming area that depicts how the real-world location will appear if one or more electronic gaming machines corresponding to the one or more corresponding virtual electronic gaming machine[[s is]] are added to the real-world location.
Claim 1, has, for example, been amended to recite elements drawn from now-canceled claim 2, which was also rejected over Eathakota. In rejecting claim 2, the Office stated:
Eathakota discloses the visualization system of claim 1, wherein the one or more
storage devices store further computer-executable instructions which, when
executed by the one or more processors, further cause the one or more processors

to: cause one or more images of a real-world electronic gaming machine to be obtained, match the real-world electronic gaming machine to a corresponding virtual electronic gaming machine in a catalogue of virtual electronic gaming
machines, and cause the corresponding virtual electronic gaming machine to be
added to the representation of the real-world location [0017].
Paragraph [0017] of Eathakota states:
A further aspect of the present disclosure includes that the virtual object is
selected from a catalogue of virtual objects in a database on the server.

There is no mention in Eathakota's paragraph [0017], or, for that matter, anywhere in Eathakota, of "caus[ing] one or more images of a real-world electronic gaming machine to be obtained" or "match[ing] the real-world electronic gaming machine to a corresponding virtual electronic gaming machine in a catalogue of virtual electronic gaming machines," as formerly recited in claim 2 and as now recited in amended claim 1. Eathakota simply does not disclose any such feature.

Applicant respectfully submits that the rejection of claim 2 was improper since Eathakota does not disclose or suggest all of the elements recited in claim 2. The Office Action simply seems to ignore these features-stating in a conclusory manner that Eathakota's paragraph [0017] discloses these features when it clearly does not.
Since claim 1 has been amended to incorporate the above-discussed features of claim 2,
Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claim 1 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 be withdrawn for at least the reasons discussed above.

Independent claims 8 and 15 recite features similar to those discussed above with respect to claim 1 (drawn from now-canceled claims 9 and 16, respectively). Applicant respectfully submits that the rejections of now-canceled claims 9 and 16 were improper for the same reasons that the rejection of now-canceled claim 2 was improper, and respectfully requests that the rejections of amended claims 8 and 15, which now recite elements from now-canceled claims 9 and 16, respectively, be withdrawn for reasons similar to those discussed above with respect to amended claim 1.

Dependent claims 3-5, 7, 10-12, 14, and 17-19 each depend, directly or indirectly, from one of claims 1, 8, or 15 and thus include all of the elements of the respective independent claim from which each depends. Applicant thus respectfully submits that claims 3-5, 7, 10-12, 14, and 17-19 are patentable over Eathakota for at least the reasons discussed above with respect to claims 1, 8 , and 15. Withdrawal of the 35 U.S.C. §103 rejections of claims 3-5, 7, 10-12, 14, and 17-19 is thus respectfully requested as well.

For at least the foregoing reasons, it is respectfully submitted that all claims are allowable.
